title: The exterior sheafification unit is bijective on affine quasi-coherent sections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $U$ an affine open of $X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $n\geq0$. Let $P_n(W)=\bigwedge^n_{\mathcal O_X(W)}F(W)$, with its canonical restrictions and sheafification $E_n$ [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. The canonical sheafification-unit map $P_n(U)\to E_n(U)$ is bijective. There is no finite-presentation or local-freeness assumption.

source.place: Lemma 26.7.2(2), lemma-widetilde-tensor; with Tag 01IA, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine, and Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves.

proof.text: Put A = Gamma(X,U), P = Gamma(F,U). The affine quasi-coherent counit identifies F on U with the associated module P. On each principal open D(f), its sections are P_f, and restriction agrees with localization.

Construct the localization comparison on pure wedges by (p_1/f^a_1) wedge ... wedge (p_n/f^a_n) mapping to (p_1 wedge ... wedge p_n)/f^(sum a_j). Multilinearity and alternation follow after bringing terms to a common denominator; changing a representative changes its numerator by a power-of-f torsion element, which becomes zero after localization. The inverse sends a pure wedge over A to the wedge of its localized entries and extends by the localization universal property. The composites agree on pure wedges, which span. These maps commute with principal restriction maps by their formula. Consequently the exterior presheaf on this basis is the associated exterior module. Sheafification preserves the identification on the basis.

Take sections over U of the resulting associated sheaf. The unit is exactly the constant-section map, hence is bijective by the affine tilde unit. In degree zero this is the identity on A, and on an empty affine open both modules are zero.
